lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p29 - Listen, point and say

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for accurate pointing to the specific food items (chicken, fish, pasta, etc.) and clear repetition of the words.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p29 - Ask and answer with What's missing?

details: Ask and answer with What's missing? develops visual memory and vocabulary recall. Students play a game where they identify which food item has been covered or removed.
Look for quick identification of the missing item and confident production of the correct food word (e.g., "It's the pizza!").

Match introduces the concept of food origins. Students draw lines connecting the food item (fruit, veg, meat) to where it comes from (tree, garden, farm, sea).
Look for logical connections: Fruit to the Tree, Vegetables to the Garden, Chicken to the Farm, Fish to the Sea.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p65 - Talk about where food comes from.

details: Talk about where food comes from provides a speaking opportunity to explain the matching activity. Students point to their work and describe the origin of the food.
Look for simple sentences or phrases linking the item to the place (e.g., "Fish comes from the water/sea").

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p29 - Say the chant

details: Say the chant consolidates the new vocabulary through rhythm and repetition. It allows students to practise natural intonation and have fun with the new food words.
Look for enthusiastic participation, clapping to the rhythm, and clear pronunciation of the food names.
